ngeneral-geography-3-55.s: Which of the following traditional Indian seasons is INCORRECTLY matched with its months?
ngeneral-geography-3-55.x: Autumn is September–October; November–December is the pre-winter season. The other three pairs are correct.

n9ee416404a7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the retreating south-west monsoon?
o: The Sun moves southward and the north-western low weakens
The westerly jet shifts north of the Himalayas
Clear skies and 'October heat' are experienced
n9ee416404a7.x: During the retreat the westerly jet returns south of the Himalayas, not north. The other three conditions accompany the retreating monsoon.

n7a97d206b25.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about rain-shadow areas in India?
o: Interior Maharashtra lies in the lee of the Western Ghats
Rayalaseema lies in the lee of the Western Ghats
Ladakh lies in the rain shadow behind the Himalayas
The Konkan coast lies in the lee of the Western Ghats
n7a97d206b25.x: The Konkan (west) coast is on the windward side of the Western Ghats and gets heavy rain. Interior Maharashtra, Rayalaseema and Ladakh are rain-shadow areas.

n5a9f3644568.s: Which of the following is NOT part of India's low-rainfall zone (less than 60 cm)?
n5a9f3644568.x: The Khasi Hills (Mawsynram) are the wettest part of India. The Thar, Kutch and Ladakh-Karakoram lie in the below-60 cm zone.

nbdc2089df72.s: The tropical easterly jet of the Indian summer monsoon extends from the South China Sea towards:
nbdc2089df72.x: The tropical easterly jet extends from the South China Sea to East Africa during the monsoon.

nb28c9307726.s: The Bay of Bengal branch of the south-west monsoon is turned westward along the Ganga plain by the:
nb28c9307726.x: After striking the Myanmar and north-eastern hills, the Bay of Bengal branch is turned westward by the Himalayas along the Ganga plain.

ncaad5f87c59.s: On which date does the south-west monsoon normally set in over Kerala?
ncaad5f87c59.x: The normal onset over Kerala is 1 June; the Andaman and Nicobar Islands get it about 25 May.

n0f4b3faefe8.s: Which place in India is the wettest, with a mean rainfall of about 1,187 cm?
n0f4b3faefe8.x: Mawsynram in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya (~1,187 cm) is the wettest place, followed by Cherrapunji (Sohra).

n544c11a5798.s: Ocean Mean Temperature (OMT) is the average temperature of the upper Indian Ocean down to the ____ isotherm.
n544c11a5798.x: OMT averages the upper Indian Ocean down to the 26 °C isotherm and predicts monsoon rain better than SST.

n7bbc1963c3a.s: Which of the following can offset the weakening effect of El Niño on the Indian monsoon?
o: A developing El Niño in the Pacific
n7bbc1963c3a.x: A positive IOD can offset El Niño; an unfavourable MJO phase stalls the monsoon instead.

n7c9cc9581e4.s: The north-east monsoon brings rain to the Coromandel (Tamil Nadu) coast during:
n7c9cc9581e4.x: The north-east monsoon rains on the Coromandel coast, Rayalaseema, Nellore and Prakasam during October–December.

na39811261b6.s: In 2026, a June rainfall deficit of about how much led the Centre to activate monsoon contingency plans?
na39811261b6.x: A 43% June deficit led to contingency planning; the IMD forecast was about 90% of the long-period average.

n551c98ecb3a.s: Andhi, the pre-monsoon dust storm of Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and western UP, spreads from the:
n551c98ecb3a.x: Andhi moves from Rajasthan (Thar) into Punjab, Haryana, Delhi and western Uttar Pradesh during March–June.

n7344c858c6d.s: Cherrapunji in Meghalaya is also known as:
n7344c858c6d.x: Cherrapunji is also called Sohra; it and Mawsynram in Meghalaya are among India's wettest places.

nf6a94561c19.s: The south-west monsoon lasts for less than 75 days in:
nf6a94561c19.x: Monsoon duration is under 75 days in western Rajasthan but over 120 days in the south-western peninsula.

n430677791a6.s: The distribution of monsoon rainfall in India is controlled mainly by:
n430677791a6.x: Relief mainly controls the distribution of monsoon rainfall, which is unequal and variable.

n077eb17a2d9.s: As per the IMD classification, the south-west monsoon season covers:
n077eb17a2d9.x: The IMD south-west monsoon season is June–September; October–December is the post-monsoon season.

n4928f00d87d.s: The hot, dry, dust-laden afternoon wind of the northern and north-western plains, also felt in Rayalaseema, is called:
n4928f00d87d.x: The Loo is a hot, dry, dusty afternoon wind of the northern and north-western plains, locally experienced in Rayalaseema.

nf3679ccbde0.s: In which year did the Ministry of Earth Sciences launch the National Monsoon Mission?
nf3679ccbde0.x: MoES launched the National Monsoon Mission in 2012, run through IITM Pune and IMD; Phase 2 began in 2017.

n5c4285b0f3b.s: 'Bardoli Chheerha' is the Assamese name for which pre-monsoon phenomenon?
n5c4285b0f3b.x: Bardoli Chheerha is Assam's name for the Kaal Baisakhi (Nor'wester) thunderstorm, also called 'tea showers'.

n11f71d49a0b.s: Mission Mausam was launched along with IMD Vision 2047 on:
n11f71d49a0b.x: Mission Mausam was launched on 14 January 2025 with IMD Vision 2047; it is implemented by IMD, NCMRWF and IITM.

nindian-geography-16-2.s: The heavy rainfall of India's western coast, caused by Arabian Sea winds striking the Western Ghats, is of which type?
nindian-geography-16-2.x: Moist Arabian Sea winds rise over the Western Ghats and drop heavy orographic rain on the west coast.

n6a73441d4bf.s: Which is the driest part of Andhra Pradesh, receiving less than 51 cm of rainfall?
n6a73441d4bf.x: The Hagari valley gets less than 51 cm; the Sileru-Sabari valleys are the wettest (about 140–152 cm).

ndisaster-management-5-2.s: In India, tornadoes peak during which period?
ndisaster-management-5-2.x: Indian tornadoes peak in the pre-monsoon months of March–May with the Nor'westers (Kal Baisakhi), mainly in the eastern States.

n040a82d12da.s: Heat waves in north-western and central India generally peak in:
n040a82d12da.x: North-western and central India are hottest from April to June, and heat waves generally peak in May–June.

n788f2062302.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about ENSO and the Indian monsoon?
o: El Niño generally weakens the Indian monsoon
La Niña generally weakens the Indian monsoon
A positive Indian Ocean Dipole can offset the effect of El Niño
El Niño is declared when the central/east equatorial Pacific is at least 0.5 °C warmer for five consecutive overlapping 3-month periods
n788f2062302.x: La Niña generally strengthens the Indian monsoon; it is El Niño that weakens it.

nadb8ecf1be1.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about flood-prone areas of India?
o: The Brahmaputra valley is a major flood-affected area
The Kosi and Ganga plains of Bihar and UP are badly flood-affected
The Brahmaputra is popularly called the 'sorrow of Bihar'
The Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri deltas are flood-prone
nadb8ecf1be1.x: The Brahmaputra is popularly associated with the 'sorrow of Assam', not Bihar. The other three are major flood-affected areas.

nfb524720c16.s: Drought defined by falling river flow and groundwater levels is called:
nfb524720c16.x: River flow and groundwater define hydrological drought; agricultural drought concerns soil moisture and meteorological drought a rain deficit.

ncb849d9fba4.s: Chronic drought in Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam is linked to groundwater depletion and the failure of the:
o: Arabian Sea branch of the monsoon
ncb849d9fba4.x: Failure of the north-east monsoon and groundwater depletion contribute to chronic drought in Rayalaseema and southern Prakasam.

ndisaster-management-8-8.s: India's national-level Disaster Management Act was enacted in:
ndisaster-management-8-8.x: The Disaster Management Act of 2005 provided national-level disaster-management legislation.

nindian-geography-16-6.s: Most of the Northern Plains and parts of Central India fall in which rainfall zone?
nindian-geography-16-6.x: The west coast and north-east are very heavy, the Western Ghats and Meghalaya heavy, and most of the Northern Plains and central India moderate.

nca13eb46f90.s: Rainfall decreases from east to west across the northern plains. Which of these cities receives the most rainfall?
nca13eb46f90.x: The east-to-west order is Kolkata > Patna > Prayagraj > Delhi > Bikaner, so Kolkata gets the most.

n2456ab1cbad.s: For a state or district, the IMD treats a rainfall departure in which band as 'normal'?
n2456ab1cbad.x: Normal is −19% to +19%; excess is +20% to +59% and large excess +60% or more.

nenvironment-8-22.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Afforestation – Planting trees on land not forested before
Reforestation – Re-establishing forest cover where it was depleted
Community participation – Planting trees on land not forested before
Social forestry – Tree development for local or community needs
nenvironment-8-22.x: Community participation means involving local people in forest management, as in Joint Forest Management; planting on never-forested land is afforestation.

nindian-geography-50-7.s: Which of the following pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Tropical Evergreen Forest – Dense, multi-layered vegetation
Tropical Thorn Forest – Deodar, pine and fir
Littoral / Tidal Forest – Mangroves and Sundari
Coniferous Forest – Deodar, pine and fir
nindian-geography-50-7.x: Thorn forests are open and stunted with long roots and thorns; deodar, pine and fir belong to coniferous forests.

nc5d38e5b58f.s: Which of the following forest type – species pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Moist deciduous – Teak, sal and mahua
Dry deciduous – Teak, sandalwood and Terminalia
Littoral or tidal – Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis
nc5d38e5b58f.x: Tidal forests have Rhizophora and Avicennia; Acacia, Ziziphus and Prosopis are thorn-forest species.

nindian-geography-50-24.s: Which of the following forest type – location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Alpine forests – Eastern slopes of the Western Ghats
Tropical Moist Deciduous – Eastern slopes of the Western Ghats
Coniferous – Temperate Himalayan belt of about 1,500–3,000 m
Tropical Evergreen – Wetter parts and coastal areas
nindian-geography-50-24.x: Alpine forests occur above about 3,000 m up to the snowline, not on the Western Ghats.

n11e126558a4.s: Besides Rajasthan and Gujarat, tropical thorn forests occur in which region of Andhra Pradesh?
n11e126558a4.x: Thorn forests occur in Rajasthan, Gujarat and Rayalaseema, in the 25–75 cm rainfall range.

n1840108d2de.s: The Sehima-Dichanthium grass type is found mainly in:
n1840108d2de.x: Sehima-Dichanthium grows on black soils; Phragmites-Saccharum is marshy, Deschampsia-Deyeuxia alpine and Bothriochloa in paddy tracts.

n5418d2e6494.s: The National Forest Policy, 1988 targets what share of India's total area under forest and tree cover?
n5418d2e6494.x: The NFP 1988 target is 33% of the total area (66% in hills and mountains); India is at 25.17% (ISFR 2023).

nd2bd50f6e64.s: A reserved forest assigned to a village community is called a:
nd2bd50f6e64.x: A village forest is a reserved forest assigned to a village community.

n52ae6fb8c82.s: The principal States of the Great Indian Bustard are:
n52ae6fb8c82.x: The Great Indian Bustard, numbering fewer than 150 birds, is associated mainly with Rajasthan and Gujarat.

nenvironment-18-1.x: The black-necked crane breeds in Ladakh; the Siberian crane wintered at Keoladeo.

nindian-geography-50-13.s: Tropical evergreen forests grow in areas receiving rainfall of:
nindian-geography-50-13.x: Evergreen forests need over 200 cm; moist deciduous 100–200 cm, dry deciduous 70–100 cm and thorn under 70 cm.

n25bce8a7e25.s: Which slopes of the Himalaya generally carry denser forests?
n25bce8a7e25.x: The southern, windward slopes generally carry denser forests than the northern slopes.

nc36b28f1cff.s: Dry alpine scrub above about 4,000 m in the Himalaya is dominated by:
nc36b28f1cff.x: Dry alpine scrub above about 4,000 m is dominated by juniper.

nindian-geography-33-4.s: Daying Ering Wildlife Sanctuary is located in which State?
nindian-geography-33-4.x: Daying Ering is in East Siang district, Arunachal Pradesh.

n6d70cfca048.s: Coringa Wildlife Sanctuary, a mangrove site near Kakinada, is in which State?
n6d70cfca048.x: Coringa WLS is near Kakinada in Andhra Pradesh; Bhitarkanika is in Odisha and Pichavaram in Tamil Nadu.

nindian-geography-23-4.s: Western Andhra Pradesh is associated with which forest type?
nindian-geography-23-4.x: Thorn forests occur in western Andhra Pradesh; evergreen forests are in the Western Ghats and mangroves in the Sundarbans.

nindian-geography-33-10.s: Rollapadu Wildlife Sanctuary in Andhra Pradesh protects the grassland habitat of the:
nindian-geography-33-10.x: Rollapadu protects the Great Indian Bustard in grassland.

n1ca0ed83a17.s: Alpine meadows above the Himalayan tree line may extend up to about:
n1ca0ed83a17.x: Alpine vegetation occurs above the tree line, and alpine meadows may extend up to about 4,750 m.

o: Long roots with thorns and spines
Leaves shed in the dry season
n8ce0af6a2d8.x: Mangroves have stilt and knee roots, may be submerged at high tide and fringe river deltas on both coasts.

n428454105c7.s: As of 2026, how many Tiger Reserves did India have?
n428454105c7.x: India had 58 Tiger Reserves (up from 9 in 1973), covering about 2.6% of its land.

n245dc0d9bde.s: According to ISFR 2023, Andhra Pradesh's mangrove cover is:
n245dc0d9bde.x: ISFR 2023 put AP's mangrove cover at 421.43 sq km, an increase of 13.01 sq km, with no very dense class.

n98c73bfdd59.s: The Forest Survey of India, which publishes the biennial ISFR, is headquartered at:
n98c73bfdd59.x: The Forest Survey of India, established in 1981, is headquartered at Dehradun.

na6e7632cd0b.s: Palamau Tiger Reserve is located in:
na6e7632cd0b.x: Palamau is in Jharkhand; Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh and Askot in Uttarakhand.

nindian-geography-49-20.s: The Muthupet mangroves are in which State?
nindian-geography-49-20.x: Pichavaram and Muthupet are in Tamil Nadu; Vembanad and Kannur are in Kerala.

nindian-geography-49-19.s: The Bhitarkanika, Devi and Dhamra mangrove areas are in:
nindian-geography-49-19.x: Bhitarkanika, Devi and Dhamra are in Odisha; Coringa lies in the Godavari delta of Andhra Pradesh.

nindian-geography-50-16.s: Open, stunted forests with long roots and thorns or spines are:
nindian-geography-50-16.x: Tropical thorn forests are open and stunted with long roots and thorns or spines.

nenvironment-12-8.s: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla Tiger Reserve is located in:
nenvironment-12-8.x: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla is in Chhattisgarh; Manas and Orang are in Assam.

nindian-geography-23-5.s: Katha is obtained from which tree of dry areas?
nindian-geography-23-5.x: Khair grows in dry or arid areas and yields katha.

nindian-geography-33-6.s: Harike Wildlife Sanctuary is located in:
nindian-geography-33-6.x: Harike is in Punjab; Sultanpur is in Haryana and Keoladeo at Bharatpur, Rajasthan.

n92e41a84adf.s: Which became India's 58th Tiger Reserve in 2025?
n92e41a84adf.x: Guru Ghasidas–Tamor Pingla was the 56th, Ratapani the 57th (2024) and Madhav the 58th (2025).

nindian-geography-50-8.s: Tropical moist deciduous forests occur in which sub-Himalayan regions?
nindian-geography-50-8.x: Moist deciduous forests grow in the Bhabar and Terai; thorn forests occur in western AP, Rajasthan and Kutch.

nindian-geography-23-12.s: Which deciduous tree is known as the 'Flame of the Forest'?
nindian-geography-23-12.x: Palash, a deciduous tree, is known as the Flame of the Forest.

n4c92646c06e.s: Under Project Cheetah, which site became the second home for cheetahs after Kuno National Park?
n4c92646c06e.x: Gandhi Sagar WLS is the second home and Veerangana Durgavati Tiger Reserve the third.

nf45760d790d.s: According to ISFR 2023, India's forest cover (excluding tree cover) is about what share of its geographical area?
nf45760d790d.x: ISFR 2023: forest cover 21.76%, tree cover 3.41%, combined 25.17%.

n6e9b84fdbf0.s: Which is the biggest forest tract of Andhra Pradesh, whose forests are mainly dry deciduous?
n6e9b84fdbf0.x: AP's forests are mainly dry deciduous, and Nallamala is the State's biggest forest tract.

n1111b14a1b5.s: In the India State of Forest Report, 'Very Dense Forest' has a canopy density of:
n1111b14a1b5.x: Very Dense Forest is 70% or more; Moderately Dense 40–70% and Open Forest 10–40%.

ne6cfa518457.s: The National Tiger Conservation Authority is a statutory body under which Act?
ne6cfa518457.x: The NTCA is a statutory body under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, headed by the Environment Minister.

n8562fec827e.s: Which is the largest of the three National Parks of Andhra Pradesh?
n8562fec827e.x: Papikonda is the largest, Rajiv Gandhi the smallest, and Sri Venkateswara (1989) was the first.

n6622ec5cae2.s: The 'Ek Ped Maa Ke Naam' campaign claimed the planting of about ____ saplings.
n6622ec5cae2.x: The campaign claimed that 140 crore saplings had been planted.

n9b60ef10578.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about protected areas under the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972?
o: A National Park provides the highest degree of protection among the categories
Grazing and private rights are not permitted in a National Park
A Wildlife Sanctuary gives a higher degree of protection than a National Park
Some activities and rights may be regulated but allowed in a Wildlife Sanctuary
n9b60ef10578.x: National Parks, not sanctuaries, provide the highest protection; sanctuaries allow some regulated activities and rights.

nindian-geography-18-6.s: Which of the following National Park – location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Sri Venkateswara – Seshachalam Hills near Tirupati
nindian-geography-18-6.x: Mouling National Park is in Arunachal Pradesh, not Assam.

n277f15d675c.s: Which of the following National Park – feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Campbell Bay – Tropical evergreen island forest
n277f15d675c.x: Dachigam is known for the Hangul (Kashmir stag); the Asiatic lion lives in Gir.

nd87c4592ab4.s: Which is Andhra Pradesh's only Biosphere Reserve?
nd87c4592ab4.x: AP has one Biosphere Reserve (Seshachalam), one tiger reserve (Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam) and one elephant reserve (Koundinya-Rayala).

nindian-geography-18-8.s: Nagarhole National Park is located in:
nindian-geography-18-8.x: Nagarhole is in Karnataka; Kanha is in Madhya Pradesh and Ranthambore and Keoladeo in Rajasthan.

nenvironment-15-4.s: Dachigam National Park is known for the:
nenvironment-15-4.x: Dachigam is known for the hangul; Kaziranga for the rhino and Gir for the Asiatic lion.

nbd8fc0b14de.s: Which sanctuary of Andhra Pradesh is a habitat of the Great Indian Bustard?
nbd8fc0b14de.x: Rollapadu WLS is one of the Great Indian Bustard's habitats; the bird numbers fewer than 150.

nbb33cc90afd.s: Balpakram National Park is located in:
nbb33cc90afd.x: Balpakram is in Meghalaya, not Manipur (PYQ 2023).

nenvironment-15-8.s: Keibul Lamjao, the floating national park on Loktak Lake, is in:
nenvironment-15-8.x: Keibul Lamjao, on Loktak Lake, is in Manipur; Intanki is in Nagaland.

nworld-geography-30-6.s: Banff National Park is located in:
nworld-geography-30-6.x: Banff is in Canada; Yellowstone is in the USA, Kruger in South Africa and Masai Mara in Kenya.

nindian-geography-27-14.s: Periyar Tiger Reserve lies in the:
nindian-geography-27-14.x: Periyar is in the Western Ghats; Nagarjunsagar–Srisailam is in the Nallamala Hills and Similipal in the Eastern Ghats.

n9e1eb3c19d9.s: Corbett, India's first national park (originally Hailey National Park), was established in:
n9e1eb3c19d9.x: Corbett was set up in 1936 as Hailey National Park; Project Tiger was launched there in 1973.

nap-geography-14-6.s: The Indira Gandhi Zoological Park of Andhra Pradesh is at:
nap-geography-14-6.x: Indira Gandhi Zoological Park is at Visakhapatnam; Sri Venkateswara Zoological Park is at Tirupati.

nindian-geography-27-18.s: Valmiki Tiger Reserve is located in:
nindian-geography-27-18.x: Valmiki is in Bihar; Nagarhole is in Karnataka and Ranthambore in Rajasthan.

nap-geography-14-8.s: Kandaleru Deer Park is located in:
nap-geography-14-8.x: Kandaleru Deer Park is in Rapur mandal, Nellore; Kotappakonda Deer Park is at Narsaraopeta, Palnadu.

nworld-geography-30-14.s: Galápagos National Park, the site of Darwin's study, is in:
nworld-geography-30-14.x: The Galápagos, in Ecuador, have endemic species and were studied by Darwin.

nworld-geography-30-5.s: Which African wildlife area is an inland delta with high wildlife density?
nworld-geography-30-5.x: The Okavango is the inland delta; Etosha is a salt pan and Virunga is known for mountain gorillas.

nenvironment-9-4.s: The Montreal Protocol entered into force in:
nenvironment-9-4.x: The Montreal Protocol came into force in 1989.

n93f217fa720.s: The Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve was established in:
n93f217fa720.x: Nilgiri was established in 1986, Nanda Devi in 1988, Gulf of Mannar in 1989 and Pachmarhi in 1999.

nenvironment-9-3.s: The Secretariat of the International Solar Alliance is located at:
nenvironment-9-3.x: The ISA is headquartered in India, with its Secretariat at Gurugram, Haryana.

nworld-geography-30-9.s: Which of the following is NOT one of the 'Big Five' of Kruger National Park?
nworld-geography-30-9.x: The Big Five are lion, leopard, elephant, rhinoceros and buffalo; the zebra is not one of them.

n1823d447e6f.s: Conservation Reserves, in which local rights remain unaffected, are declared by the:
n1823d447e6f.x: Conservation Reserves are declared by the State on government land; local rights are unaffected and panchayats sit on management committees.

n4469c92da22.s: Mahuadanr Wildlife Sanctuary is located in Latehar district of:
n4469c92da22.x: Mahuadanr WLS is in Latehar, Jharkhand; Askot and Binsar are in Uttarakhand.

n00bf43e9d05.s: Keoladeo National Park is located in which district of Rajasthan?
n00bf43e9d05.x: Keoladeo is at Bharatpur; Sariska is associated with Alwar.

ncd150836c0e.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about wildlife sanctuaries and their key species?
o: National Chambal protects the gharial and Gangetic dolphin
Bhitarkanika is known for saltwater crocodiles and mangroves
Gahirmatha is known for olive ridley mass nesting
Gir, the only natural home of the Asiatic lion, is in Odisha
ncd150836c0e.x: Gir is in Gujarat, not Odisha. Bhitarkanika and Gahirmatha are the Odisha sites.

n31c3f449338.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about elephant reserves (ERs) in India?
o: Odisha's ERs are Mayurbhanj, Mahanadi and Sambalpur
ERs are notified only in areas outside tiger reserves
Stored carbon in ERs has risen by about 38%
n31c3f449338.x: Elephant reserves overlap tiger reserves, sanctuaries and reserved forests, so they are not limited to areas outside tiger reserves.

nccb9de262dd.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Ramsar definition of a wetland?
o: It includes marshes, fens and peatlands
It includes fresh, brackish or salt water
It covers only natural water bodies, not artificial ones
It includes marine water up to 6 metres deep at low tide
nccb9de262dd.x: The Ramsar definition covers both natural and artificial water bodies.

n8b657301478.s:
Assertion (A): The Bar-headed goose is seen in India during winter.
Reason (R): It breeds on high lakes of Central Asia and crosses the Himalaya to winter in India.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n8b657301478.x: The goose breeds on high Central Asian lakes and crosses the Himalaya to winter in India, which explains its winter presence; it is one of the highest-flying birds.

nindian-geography-42-16.s: Pulicat Bird Sanctuary lies on the border of:
nindian-geography-42-16.x: Pulicat is on the AP–Tamil Nadu border; Kolleru is in AP, Bharatpur in Rajasthan and Nalsarovar in Gujarat.

n57dd9b74bc5.s: The Amur falcon, which makes the longest raptor migration, winters in:
n57dd9b74bc5.x: It migrates from south-east Siberia and northern China to southern Africa, stopping over in Nagaland in October–November.

nindian-geography-42-15.s: Nelapattu Bird Sanctuary is located in:
nindian-geography-42-15.x: Nelapattu is in Andhra Pradesh; Vedanthangal is in Tamil Nadu, Ranganathittu in Karnataka and Sultanpur in Haryana.

ne45e1f258c4.x: Project Elephant began in February 1992; it has 33 elephant reserves in 14 States.

nindian-geography-42-19.s: Which of the following bird sanctuaries does NOT lie, even partly, in Andhra Pradesh?
nindian-geography-42-19.x: Vedanthangal is in Tamil Nadu; Nelapattu, Kolleru and Pulicat (on the border) include Andhra Pradesh.

nindian-geography-42-18.s: Which of the following bird sanctuaries is NOT in Kerala?
nindian-geography-42-18.x: Ranganathittu is in Karnataka; Kumarakom, Thattekad and Mangalavanam are in Kerala.

nb9914569e67.s: In which year was the Ramsar Convention on wetlands adopted at Ramsar, Iran?
nb9914569e67.x: The Convention was adopted in 1971 at Ramsar, Iran; India joined in 1982.

n5251d027397.s: Project Lion, for the Asiatic lion of Gir, was launched in:
n5251d027397.x: Project Lion was launched in 2020; Gir in Gujarat is the only natural home of the Asiatic lion.

o: Ramsar sites whose ecological character is threatened or undergoing adverse change
Wetlands proposed for future Ramsar listing
n97b18890ff7.x: The Montreux Record lists threatened Ramsar sites; India's entries are Keoladeo and Loktak.

n690511194e1.s: Why is the possibility of human–tiger conflict in India growing?
o: All tigers now live within notified Tiger Reserves
Reserve boundaries have expanded to cover all tiger habitat
A growing share of tigers now live outside notified reserves
Tigers outside reserves are no longer part of conservation landscapes
n690511194e1.x: A growing share of India's tigers lives outside notified reserves, raising the possibility of conflict with people.

nf5e23477ca4.s: Andhra Pradesh's only elephant reserve, which includes Koundinya WLS, is:
nf5e23477ca4.x: AP's one elephant reserve is Rayala (incl. Koundinya WLS); its biosphere reserve is Seshachalam and its tiger reserve NSTR.

n659807cdcce.s: India, a key wintering ground on the Central Asian Flyway, hosted CMS COP13 in 2020 at:
n659807cdcce.x: India hosted the 13th Conference of the Convention on Migratory Species at Gandhinagar in 2020.

n6ee79cce9be.s: How many listed Ramsar sites does Odisha have?
n6ee79cce9be.x: Odisha has six: Chilika, Bhitarkanika, Ansupa, Tampara, Hirakud and Satkosia Gorge.

na9f78d48b87.s: Which of the following soil-conservation method – function pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Contour ploughing – Ploughing along contour lines to slow runoff
Terracing – Steps cut on steep slopes
Check dams – Tree rows that reduce wind speed
Shelter belts – Tree rows that reduce wind speed
na9f78d48b87.x: Check dams trap sediment and check gully growth; tree rows that cut wind speed are shelter belts.

n4ea8f02abba.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about factors controlling soil erosion?
o: Slope gradient influences the rate of erosion
Vegetation cover and land use influence erosion
Total annual rainfall is always more important than rainfall intensity
Soil type and texture influence erosion
n4ea8f02abba.x: Rainfall intensity generally matters more than total annual rainfall.

n453757bd37b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about conservation agriculture?
o: It may involve minimum or zero tillage
Crop residue is retained as soil cover
It requires complete removal of crop residues
n453757bd37b.x: Conservation agriculture retains crop residues; removing them completely is contrary to the practice.

nindian-geography-19-6.s: Which of the following soil – region pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Laterite soil – Northern Plains and river valleys
Alluvial soil – Northern Plains and river valleys
Red soil – Crystalline eastern and southern Peninsula
nindian-geography-19-6.x: Laterite soil occurs on the summits of the Western and Eastern Ghats; the Northern Plains have alluvial soil.

na2dbacd80af.s: The Integrated Watershed Management Programme (IWMP) began in:
na2dbacd80af.x: IWMP started in 2009-10 and was merged into the Watershed Development Component of PMKSY in 2015-16.

nenvironment-28-8.s: The remedy matched with deforestation is:
nenvironment-28-8.x: Deforestation pairs with afforestation; soil erosion with soil stabilisation, habitat destruction with restoration and biodiversity loss with conservation.

n792e55fefe9.s: Peaty and marshy soils, found in Alappuzha-Kottayam and the Sundarbans, are typically:
n792e55fefe9.x: Peaty soils form under heavy rain and waterlogging; they are black, heavy and highly acidic, not alkaline.

n153ccbac8ac.s: Karewa soils of the Kashmir Valley are famous for the cultivation of:
n153ccbac8ac.x: Karewas (old lake-bed deposits) are famous for saffron, especially around Pampore.

n7a9ecd170a7.s: The red colour of red soils is due to:
n7a9ecd170a7.x: Iron oxide makes these soils red; they look yellow when hydrated. They form from granite and gneiss.

n08eb7e2c953.s: Which soil is known for deep summer cracks and its 'self-ploughing' character?
n08eb7e2c953.x: Black soil has over 62% clay, high moisture retention, deep summer cracks and a self-ploughing character.

nea95fcb16f9.s: Black (regur) soil is formed mainly from the weathering of:
nea95fcb16f9.x: Black soil comes from weathered Deccan Trap basalt and is neutral to alkaline.

nd753b7b5415.s: Reh, kallar and usar are local names for which soils?
nd753b7b5415.x: Reh, kallar and usar are saline/alkaline soils formed by over-irrigation and poor drainage.

n9eb19fc6c18.s: The Soil Health Card scheme was launched on 19 February 2015 at:
n9eb19fc6c18.x: It was launched at Suratgarh, Rajasthan; cards are issued every two years and the slogan is 'Swasth Dharaa, Khet Haraa'.

n92bc077fec1.s: When adequately manured, laterite soil supports which group of crops?
n92bc077fec1.x: Laterite soil can support tea, coffee, rubber and cashew when adequately manured.

n7e5332c0e42.s: Very deep black soils are found in the:
n7e5332c0e42.x: Very deep black soils lie in the north-western Deccan Plateau.

nindian-geography-19-9.s: Which of the following crops is NOT typically grown on alluvial soil?
nindian-geography-19-9.x: Coffee is grown on the red and laterite soils of the Western Ghats; wheat, rice and sugarcane suit alluvial soil.

n2cf70253f25.s: Which is the final, most advanced stage of water erosion?
n2cf70253f25.x: Water erosion progresses from splash to sheet, then rill and finally gully erosion.

n0cc2cfcd2fd.s: Which soil order covers the largest share of India's area?
n0cc2cfcd2fd.x: Inceptisols cover 39.7%, ahead of Entisols (28.1%), Alfisols (13.6%) and Vertisols (8.5%).

n7b0451f5e8c.s: Red soils cover about what share of Andhra Pradesh's cultivated area?
n7b0451f5e8c.x: Red soils cover about 60%; black soils about 25%, deltaic alluvium 5–6% and laterite about 1%.

n23d1aba3196.s: The FAO 2026 assessment found sustainable soil-management practices worsening in about what share of assessments?
n23d1aba3196.x: Practices were worsening in 58% of assessments and improving in only about 10%.

n7bb1e5d86ef.s: Residual (in situ) soils dominate which part of India?
n7bb1e5d86ef.x: Residual soils dominate Peninsular India, while drifted (ex situ) soils dominate North India.

nce701138deb.s: How many major soil types are generally recognised in India's classification?
nce701138deb.x: Eight: alluvial, black, red and yellow, laterite, arid, saline and alkaline, peaty and marshy, and forest and mountain soils.

nc2e96892d73.s: Arid (desert) soil is sandy and deficient in:
nc2e96892d73.x: Arid soil is sandy and poor in nitrogen and humus, improves with irrigation, and has kankar at lower depths.

n1c88665bc6d.s: Which of the following is a role of soil organic carbon?
n1c88665bc6d.x: Soil organic carbon binds particles into aggregates, raises infiltration and feeds microbes.

nbebde6680a5.s: The RUSLE model is used to predict:
nbebde6680a5.x: RUSLE predicts long-term water erosion on slopes; ICAR has prepared national C- and P-factor maps for it.

nap-geography-6-12.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh mineral pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Major limestone centres – Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla (Kurnool)
nap-geography-6-12.x: Barytes is linked to the Kadapa rocks; Bethamcherla and Koilakuntla are the main limestone centres.

n275af77783c.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Swarnagiri Gold Mine?
o: It was renamed from the Jonnagiri Gold Mine
It is located in Tuggali mandal of Kurnool district
It belongs to the Jonnagiri greenstone belt
It is an underground mine operated under a ten-year lease
n275af77783c.x: Swarnagiri is an open-pit mine with a 30-year lease, not an underground mine on a ten-year lease.

n79487e0acc7.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the National Critical Mineral Mission?
o: It targets 1,200 domestic exploration projects by 2030-31
It bars PSUs and private firms from acquiring mineral assets abroad
It aims to acquire 50 overseas mineral assets
A national stockpile is one of its tools
n79487e0acc7.x: The mission supports PSU and private acquisition of mineral assets abroad.

n88f93c74205.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the MMDR Act, 1957?
o: It is administered by the Ministry of Mines
It excludes petroleum, natural gas and atomic minerals
Major minerals in the First Schedule are regulated by the Centre
Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the Centre
n88f93c74205.x: Minor minerals such as building stone, gravel and sand are regulated by the States.

nindian-geography-43-12.s: Which of the following rock system – location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Dharwar – Oldest metamorphic schist belts, rich in iron ore and gold
Gondwana – Oldest metamorphic schist belts, rich in iron ore and gold
nindian-geography-43-12.x: Gondwana rocks lie in the Damodar, Son, Mahanadi and Godavari basins; the oldest schist belts are Dharwar.

nb925cc134cd.s:
Assertion (A): Balaghat and Chhindwara are important manganese-bearing areas of Madhya Pradesh.
Reason (R): Sundargarh and Kendujhar are important manganese-bearing areas of Odisha.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
nb925cc134cd.x: Both are true manganese facts, but the Odisha deposits do not explain the Madhya Pradesh deposits.

nindian-geography-8-16.s: Which of the following is still worked as India's main gold mine?
nindian-geography-8-16.x: Hutti in Karnataka is India's main working gold mine; the Kolar Gold Fields closed in 2001.

n77ae85b4f9d.s: Sona Pahar in Meghalaya is an important occurrence of:
n77ae85b4f9d.x: Sona Pahar is associated with sillimanite; Lapsa Buru with kyanite and the Cuddapah basin with asbestos.

nae773585877.s: The North-Western (Aravalli) mineral belt is known mainly for:
o: Non-ferrous minerals such as copper and lead-zinc
nae773585877.x: The North-Western belt is known for non-ferrous minerals, plus gypsum, salt, limestone and Gujarat's petroleum.

n8c91e841121.s: Which region of India is poor in minerals because it is made of recent alluvium?
n8c91e841121.x: The Gangetic plains are recent alluvium and poor in minerals, while the peninsular plateau is mineral-rich.

n98f490fa8df.s: The Dharwar system of Andhra Pradesh is associated mainly with:
n98f490fa8df.x: The Dharwar system (over 2,500 million years old) holds iron ore and gold; barytes and asbestos belong to the Cuddapah basin.

nce08831d181.s: Mica is used in the electrical and electronic industries because it is:
nce08831d181.x: Mica is valued as an insulator, not a conductor; it occurs in pegmatite veins in granite, gneiss and schist.

n903dda7e74f.s: The royalty formula upheld by the Supreme Court in July 2026 uses an Average Sale Price that includes:
n903dda7e74f.x: The upheld formula's Average Sale Price includes royalty, DMF and NMET; royalty itself is not a tax (MADA v. SAIL, 2024).

nchemistry-3-77.s: Thorium occurs in Indian beach sands in the form of:
nchemistry-3-77.x: Thorium occurs as monazite and titanium as ilmenite in beach sands.

n9e6b83711d7.s: Araku, Ananthagiri, Chintapalli and Paderu in Andhra Pradesh are known for deposits of:
n9e6b83711d7.x: These Eastern Ghats agency areas hold bauxite; mining clashes with PVTG rights and Eastern Ghats ecology.

n8325e9414e2.s: The beach sands of Srikakulam and Visakhapatnam are known for:
o: Ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite
n8325e9414e2.x: These beach sands contain ilmenite, rutile, zircon, garnet and monazite.

n6aa4a4638d0.s: The Zawar mines are associated with:
n6aa4a4638d0.x: Zawar is associated with lead-zinc; Koderma with mica, Bailadila with iron ore and Khetri with copper.

nb5b41d08fc7.s: In the South-Western Plateau mineral belt, Kerala is noted for:
nb5b41d08fc7.x: The belt spans Karnataka, Goa, the TN uplands and Kerala; Kerala is noted for monazite.

nchemistry-1-5.s: Haematite and magnetite are ores of:
nchemistry-1-5.x: Iron comes from haematite and magnetite; aluminium from bauxite, copper from chalcopyrite and zinc from zinc blende.

n5776c1dab98.s: The rare-earth corridors proposed in the Union Budget 2026–27 cover Odisha, Kerala, Tamil Nadu and:
n5776c1dab98.x: The proposed rare-earth corridors cover Odisha, Kerala, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu.

nindian-geography-8-1.s: Panna in Madhya Pradesh is known for:
nindian-geography-8-1.x: Panna is known for diamonds; Koderma for mica, Keonjhar for manganese and Sukinda for chromite.

n085d3ac401c.s: Bauxite deposits are generally formed by:
n085d3ac401c.x: Residual weathering may produce laterite-linked bauxite; veins/lodes give tin, copper, zinc and lead.

nindian-geography-43-13.s: Gondwana rocks are the main source of India's:
nindian-geography-43-13.x: Gondwana rocks hold coal; Dharwar rocks copper, Tertiary rocks petroleum and gas, and metamorphic rocks garnet.

nchemistry-1-18.s: Rock salt is an ore of:
nchemistry-1-18.x: Sodium comes from rock salt; potassium from sylvine and carnallite, magnesium from magnesite and calcium from limestone.

nindian-geography-8-22.s: Mainpat in Surguja district of Chhattisgarh is known for:
nindian-geography-8-22.x: Surguja has bauxite at Mainpat; Dantewada in Chhattisgarh has tin.

nchemistry-3-38.x: Cinnabar is mercury sulphide; galena is lead, chalcopyrite copper and zinc blende zinc.

nchemistry-3-46.s: The chemical formula of dolomite is:
nchemistry-3-46.x: Dolomite is CaMg(CO₃)₂; magnesite is MgCO₃, rock salt NaCl and carnallite KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O.

nchemistry-1-10.s: Which of the following is a sulphide mineral?
nchemistry-1-10.x: Galena (PbS) is a sulphide; smithsonite and calcite are carbonates and cassiterite an oxide.

nchemistry-3-43.s: The chemical formula of iron pyrites is:
nchemistry-3-43.x: Iron pyrites is FeS₂; magnetite is Fe₃O₄, siderite FeCO₃ and limonite FeO(OH)·nH₂O.

n190b66671f9.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh is one of India's major mica belts?
n190b66671f9.x: The major mica belts are Nellore, Koderma–Gaya–Hazaribagh and Ajmer–Bhilwara.

n7a486aaf99b.s: The Khetri copper area is located in:
n7a486aaf99b.x: Khetri (Jhunjhunu) is in Rajasthan; Malanjkhand is the copper area of Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand's copper is in Singhbhum.

nchemistry-3-7.s: Which of the following metals is NOT found in the free (native) state?
nchemistry-3-7.x: Aluminium is very reactive and found combined, mainly as bauxite; gold, silver and platinum occur native.

nindian-geography-8-6.s: Bastar, Bilaspur, Dantewada and Jashpur are bauxite areas of:
nindian-geography-8-6.x: All four are bauxite areas of Chhattisgarh.

nadfcb1f44a1.s: The Critical Mineral Recycling Incentive Scheme, covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap, is a:
nadfcb1f44a1.x: It is a Central Sector scheme covering e-waste, lithium-ion batteries and other scrap.

nf93af26d410.s: Over 90% of India's coking-coal reserves are in:
nf93af26d410.x: Over 90% of coking-coal reserves are in Jharia; it is a Critical and Strategic Mineral under the MMDR Act, 1957.

nchemistry-3-24.s: Which of the following is NOT an ore of manganese?
nchemistry-3-24.x: Ilmenite is a titanium ore; pyrolusite, manganite and hausmannite are manganese ores.

nindian-geography-8-7.s: The Noamundi iron-ore area is located in:
nindian-geography-8-7.x: Noamundi and Singhbhum are in Jharkhand; Badampahar is in Odisha, Bailadila in Chhattisgarh and Kudremukh in Karnataka.

nc093fbb1de7.s: Under the recent MMDR amendment, States must approve adding a critical mineral to a lease within:
nc093fbb1de7.x: States must approve within 30 days; the amendment also removed captive-sale limits.

nindian-geography-43-16.s: Which rock basin of Andhra Pradesh is associated with barytes, asbestos, diamond and uranium?
nindian-geography-43-16.x: The Cuddapah basin has barytes, asbestos, copper, iron, lead, diamond and uranium.

nindian-geography-8-13.s: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are bauxite areas of:
nindian-geography-8-13.x: Koraput, Lanjigarh and Kalahandi are Odisha bauxite areas.

nchemistry-3-70.s: Which of the following metals is too reactive ever to be found free in nature?
nchemistry-3-70.x: K, Na, Ca, Mg and Al are at the top of the reactivity series and never occur free; Au, Ag and Pt occur native.

nindian-geography-8-4.s: Digboi in Assam is associated with:
nindian-geography-8-4.x: Digboi is an oilfield; Zawar has zinc and Tummalapalle in AP has uranium.

nchemistry-3-22.x: Carnallite (KCl·MgCl₂·6H₂O) is an ore of both potassium and magnesium.

nchemistry-3-47.s: The chemical formula of gypsum is:
nchemistry-3-47.x: Gypsum is CaSO₄·2H₂O; limestone and calcite are CaCO₃ and fluorspar CaF₂.

nchemistry-3-12.s: Bailadila in Chhattisgarh is famous for high-grade:
nchemistry-3-12.x: Bailadila is famous for high-grade haematite; ilmenite occurs in beach sands from Kerala to Odisha.

nworld-geography-4-8.s: China, the top producer of rare earth elements, accounts for about what share of rare-earth mining?
nworld-geography-4-8.x: China is the top rare-earth producer with about 70% of mining.

nindian-geography-8-5.s: Kaimur–Rohtas in Bihar is associated with:
nindian-geography-8-5.x: Kaimur–Rohtas in Bihar has limestone; Rajasthan has gypsum.

n807c33ab4fb.s: India's first list of critical minerals, released by the Ministry of Mines in June 2023, contained how many minerals?
n807c33ab4fb.x: The June 2023 list named 30 critical minerals; 50 is the overseas-asset target of the Critical Mineral Mission.

nb6e27a5373a.s: Which Article of the Constitution vests offshore minerals in the Union?
nb6e27a5373a.x: Article 297 vests offshore minerals in the Union; the 2023 amendment allows production leases only through auction.

n4294218f6db.s: With respect to iron ore, India is:
o: Dependent on imports for almost all its needs
n4294218f6db.x: India is self-sufficient in iron ore and a net exporter (about 46 million tonnes exported in 2023–24).

ne7e20176247.s: Which of the following hazard – region pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
ne7e20176247.x: Kutch is among the Zone V (highest) earthquake-prone regions, not Zone II.

n8779dbd19f2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the proposed revision of India's seismic zoning map?
o: It was based on Probabilistic Seismic Hazard Assessment
It was implemented nationwide in March 2026
It used PGA values of 0.15–0.75 g
The four-zone IS 1893 map (Zones II–V) still applies
n8779dbd19f2.x: The Centre rolled the revision back in March 2026 after criticism of its methodology and cost, so it was not implemented.

n841c3b96a41.s:
Assertion (A): About 40 million hectares of India is flood-prone.
Reason (R): Nearly 40% of India's land area is flood-prone.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
n841c3b96a41.x: About 40 million ha is flood-prone, but that is about 12% of the land, not 40%.

n5371a209688.s: Which of the following region – reason for landslide-proneness pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Himalaya – Young, fragile geology and active tectonics
Western Ghats and Nilgiris – Permafrost and glacial action
North-East – Steep slopes and heavy rain
Western Ghats – Steep escarpments and orographic rain
n5371a209688.x: The Western Ghats and Nilgiris are landslide-prone because of steep escarpments and orographic rain, not permafrost.

n9a11f45132d.s: The Indian Tsunami Early Warning Centre, operating since 2007, is located at:
n9a11f45132d.x: The centre is at INCOIS, Hyderabad, under the Ministry of Earth Sciences.

ndisaster-management-18-16.s: Rock bolting, wire mesh, drainage improvement and slope grading are which type of landslide-mitigation measure?
ndisaster-management-18-16.x: All four are structural landslide-mitigation measures.

ndisaster-management-23-7.s: The Asian Disaster Preparedness Centre (ADPC) is located in:
ndisaster-management-23-7.x: ADPC is in Bangkok; ADRC is in Kobe, UNESCO-IOC in Paris and ITIC in Honolulu.

ndisaster-management-23-6.s: Which body is the focal point for the Sendai Framework and global disaster risk reduction?
ndisaster-management-23-6.x: The UN Office for Disaster Risk Reduction (UNDRR) is the focal point for Sendai and global DRR.

ndisaster-management-23-11.s: The IOC-coordinated Indian Ocean Tsunami Warning System was established after the Indian Ocean tsunami of:
ndisaster-management-23-11.x: The system was set up after the 2004 tsunami, with regional centres in India, Indonesia, Australia and others.

ndisaster-management-18-5.s: Landslide Hazard Zonation mapping is classed as which type of mitigation measure?
ndisaster-management-18-5.x: Hazard zonation mapping is non-structural; retaining walls are structural and hill building codes regulatory.

ndisaster-management-23-21.s: The Asian Disaster Reduction Center (ADRC), which shares information and research on disasters, is located at:
ndisaster-management-23-21.x: ADRC is at Kobe, Japan; ADPC, which builds capacity, is in Bangkok.

n8ad7b10abf2.s: After the 1993 Killari earthquake, the 2002 seismic-zone revision merged old Zone I into:
n8ad7b10abf2.x: Killari struck a low-risk area, leading to the 2002 revision in which old Zone I was merged into Zone II.

n80f573ab5b5.s: How many seismic zones does India's official IS 1893 (BIS) zoning map presently have?
n80f573ab5b5.x: The official map has four zones: II, III, IV and V.

n9caed985277.s: In India's building-safety standards, IS 13920 covers:
n9caed985277.x: IS 13920 covers ductile detailing; IS 1893 covers seismic design criteria, and the National Building Code also applies.

nfa1a550df59.s: The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) is chaired by the:
nfa1a550df59.x: APSDMA is chaired by the Chief Minister and runs the State Emergency Operations Centre.

nac94f016892.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Polavaram-related territorial changes of Andhra Pradesh?
o: Seven Polavaram-affected mandals were transferred from Khammam to Andhra Pradesh
The transfer was effected through the 2014 Polavaram ordinance and amendment
Polavaram district was created mainly to manage the drought-prone Rayalaseema uplands
Chinturu division is now part of Polavaram district
nac94f016892.x: Polavaram district was created for the rehabilitation and resettlement of Polavaram-project villages, not for Rayalaseema.

n04a875fff54.s: As on 31 December 2025, how many districts did Andhra Pradesh have?
n04a875fff54.x: AP had 28 districts, including Markapuram (from western Prakasam) and Polavaram.

n55aa339eba3.s: According to the Government of AP, the present area of Andhra Pradesh (about 4.96% of India) is:
n55aa339eba3.x: The GoAP figure is 1,62,970 sq km; undivided AP covered about 2,75,000 sq km and 1,60,205 sq km is an older base figure.

nap-geography-27-7.s: YSR (Kadapa), Annamayya, Tirupati and Chittoor districts belong to which region of Andhra Pradesh?
nap-geography-27-7.x: All four districts are in Rayalaseema.

n50c8ddaaca5.s: After Jammu and Kashmir became a Union Territory in 2019, Andhra Pradesh became the ____ largest State by area.
n50c8ddaaca5.x: AP was eighth until 31 October 2019 and became seventh after J&K became a UT.

ndebf8ff960e.s: In the 2022 district arrangement, how many districts did Rayalaseema have?
ndebf8ff960e.x: Uttarandhra had 6 districts, the rest of Coastal Andhra 12 and Rayalaseema 8.

nap-geography-1-2.s: Asia's first rubber dam was built on which river, a tributary of the Nagavali?
nap-geography-1-2.x: Asia's first rubber dam was built on the Janjavathi, a tributary of the Nagavali.

n8148ae23a9d.s: The Uttarandhra region of Andhra Pradesh is also called:
n8148ae23a9d.x: Uttarandhra (Kalinga Andhra) comprises ASR, Anakapalli, Parvathipuram Manyam, Visakhapatnam, Vizianagaram and Srikakulam.

nd28488bb4ea.s: Andhra State, formed on 1 October 1953, had its capital at:
nd28488bb4ea.x: Andhra State was formed on 1 October 1953 with Kurnool as capital; Andhra Pradesh was formed on 1 November 1956.

n28c65c7655d.s: Which region of Andhra Pradesh holds the river deltas, most of the farm output and the highest population density?
n28c65c7655d.x: Coastal Andhra is marked by its deltas, dominant share of farm output and highest population density.

nap-geography-14-1.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh bird sanctuary – habitat pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Kolleru & Atapaka – Large freshwater lake between the Godavari and Krishna deltas
Kondakarla Ava – Freshwater lake near Anakapalle
nap-geography-14-1.x: Rollapadu is dry grassland (rangeland) for the Great Indian Bustard, not a lagoon.

nap-geography-21-6.s: Which of the following Andhra Pradesh waterfall pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Talakona Falls – Tallest waterfall in Andhra Pradesh
Ethipothala Falls – Flows into the Nagarjuna Sagar reservoir
nap-geography-21-6.x: Kailasakona is near Nagari and linked to the Kailasanatha Swamy temple; Katiki is the Araku-region fall.

nindian-geography-12-7.s: Which of the following hill range – location pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Biligirirangan Hills – Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
Kaimur Range – Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh and Bihar
Nallamalai Hills – Andhra Pradesh and Telangana
nindian-geography-12-7.x: The Biligirirangan Hills are in south-east Karnataka.

n2af72194d7e.s: The Simhachalam and Yarada hills are located in which district?
n2af72194d7e.x: Simhachalam and Yarada are in Visakhapatnam; Velikonda is in SPSR Nellore–Tirupati and Palakonda in YSR Kadapa–Tirupati.

nabb9811bb3a.s: Which district of Andhra Pradesh has the longest coastline (about 193 km)?
nabb9811bb3a.x: Srikakulam has the longest district coast (193 km) and West Godavari the shortest (23 km).

n79027581f43.s: The Eastern Ghats join the Western Ghats near the:
n79027581f43.x: The Eastern Ghats, starting with Mahendragiri in the north and running through the Javadi and Shevaroy hills, join the Western Ghats near the Nilgiris.

nindian-geography-28-3.s: The Shevaroy Hills are located in:
nindian-geography-28-3.x: The Shevaroy are in Salem; the Javadi in Vellore–Tiruvannamalai and the Nandi Hills in Karnataka.

nap-geography-21-4.x: Ethipothala is near Macherla; Katiki is near Araku, Kailasakona near Nagari and Rampa near Rampachodavaram.

n56a844cbc92.s: The figure of 1,60,205 sq km for Andhra Pradesh refers to its area:
o: After the 7 Polavaram mandals were added
Left after the 2014 bifurcation, before the Polavaram mandals were added
At the formation of Andhra State in 1953
n56a844cbc92.x: 1,60,205 sq km is the post-bifurcation area before the 7 Polavaram mandals were added; the present area is about 1,62,970 sq km.

ne144d74c1a5.s: The Eastern Ghats are made mainly of:
ne144d74c1a5.x: The Eastern Ghats are made mainly of Archaean khondalite and charnockite, over 2.5 billion years old.

ne37ed44df9b.s: What is the height of Galikonda peak in the Eastern Ghats?
ne37ed44df9b.x: Galikonda is 1,643 m; Arma Konda is 1,680 m, Sintram Gutta 1,620 m and Mahendragiri 1,501 m.

ne0229b7b53e.s: Which State borders Andhra Pradesh on the south?
ne0229b7b53e.x: Tamil Nadu is on the south; Odisha and Chhattisgarh on the north, and Karnataka and Telangana on the west.

n864a949fe5a.s: 'Konaseema' refers to the delta of which river?
n864a949fe5a.x: Konaseema is the Godavari delta; the Krishna delta covers Krishna, Guntur and Bapatla districts.

nap-geography-14-13.s: The Uppalapadu Protection Centre in Andhra Pradesh is noted as a nesting site for:
o: Great Indian Bustards and lesser floricans
Spot-billed storks, pelicans and black-headed ibises
nap-geography-14-13.x: Spot-billed storks, cattle egrets, pelicans and black-headed ibises nest at Uppalapadu.

nfdfd7510152.s: Kolleru, lying between the Godavari and Krishna deltas, is a:
nfdfd7510152.x: Kolleru is a freshwater lake between the two deltas; Pulicat is a saltwater lagoon shared with Tamil Nadu.

n75713c61bd4.s: According to NCCR (Aug 2026), which is Andhra Pradesh's worst coastal-erosion spot?
n75713c61bd4.x: Uppada in Kakinada district is AP's worst erosion spot; nationally 38% of the east coast is eroding against 30% of the west coast.

nap-geography-21-5.s: Which waterfall of Andhra Pradesh is linked to the Kailasanatha Swamy temple?
nap-geography-21-5.x: Kailasakona, not Kothapalli, is linked to Kailasanatha Swamy.

nap-geography-8-5.s: The southern section of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh is called the:
nap-geography-8-5.x: The northern section is the Eastern Ranges and the southern section the Kadapa Ranges.

nap-geography-14-5.s: Besides the Great Indian Bustard, Rollapadu Bird Sanctuary protects the:
nap-geography-14-5.x: Rollapadu is associated with the Great Indian Bustard and the lesser florican.

nap-geography-9-3.s: The Ganjikunta pass in the Eastern Ghats links which two hill ranges?
nap-geography-9-3.x: Ganjikunta is a notable pass because it connects the Seshachalam and Nallamala sections.

nb081924215a.s: From the coast towards the interior, the physiographic regions of Andhra Pradesh are:
o: Western plateau – Eastern Ghats – Coastal plains
Eastern Ghats – Coastal plains – Western plateau
Coastal plains – Eastern Ghats – Western plateau
Coastal plains – Western plateau – Eastern Ghats
nb081924215a.x: From east to west the sequence is Coastal plains, Eastern Ghats and Western plateau.

n70fa0329e19.s: According to the recalculated measurement, the coastline of Andhra Pradesh is about:
n70fa0329e19.x: The recalculated AP coastline is 1,053.07 km, third after Gujarat and Tamil Nadu; 974 km is the older figure.

ndfe81c53f46.s: The Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve was established in:
ndfe81c53f46.x: NSTR was established in 1983 and covers about 3,728 sq km in the Nallamala hills of AP.

na886b3b23ee.s: Arma Konda (1,680 m) in the ASR district of Andhra Pradesh is also called:
na886b3b23ee.x: Arma Konda, also known as Sitamma Konda, is recorded as 1,680 m high in ASR district.

n0750ed264fe.s: Under the proposed programme from September 2026, gaur are to be translocated from Central India to:
n0750ed264fe.x: Gaur are to be moved from Central India to NSTR and Nallamala from September 2026 with WII support.

nap-geography-14-10.s: Greater flamingos in Andhra Pradesh are associated with which sanctuary?
nap-geography-14-10.x: Greater flamingos belong to Pulicat, not Kolleru; Kolleru has painted storks, grey pelicans and glossy ibises.

n75caa445bdf.s: The Coringa mangroves near Kakinada lie at the estuary of the:
n75caa445bdf.x: Coringa is at the Godavari estuary near Kakinada; the Krishna Wildlife Sanctuary covers the Krishna estuary mangroves.

ncf7289391d1.s: The Seshachalam hills are a part of the:
ncf7289391d1.x: Seshachalam belongs to the Eastern Ghats; calling it part of the Nilgiris is incorrect.

nb30a7287a60.s: The Erramala hills form the water divide between:
o: The Krishna basin to the north and the Penna basin to the south
The Penna basin to the north and the Krishna basin to the south
The Bay of Bengal and the Eastern Ghats
nb30a7287a60.x: Erramala (Kurnool–Nandyal) divides the Krishna basin in the north from the Penna basin in the south.

na6799c12d7f.s: The Andhra coast north of the Krishna river is called the:
na6799c12d7f.x: North of the Krishna is the Northern Circars coast; south of it is the Coromandel coast.

n472e5af747d.s: The Eastern Ghats are best described as a:
o: Discontinuous, eroded hill system cut by major rivers
Volcanic chain with no river gaps
Recent block mountain parallel to the west coast
n472e5af747d.x: The Eastern Ghats are discontinuous, eroded hills dissected by the Mahanadi, Godavari, Krishna and Kaveri.

n609cc0b94d8.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the river-water provisions of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014?
o: Schedule 11 places drinking water above irrigation, and irrigation above power
The Apex Council is chaired by the Union Water Resources Minister with the CMs of AP and Telangana
The Krishna River Management Board has its headquarters in Telangana
The Godavari River Management Board has its headquarters in Telangana
n609cc0b94d8.x: KRMB has its headquarters in Andhra Pradesh; it is GRMB that is in Telangana.

nap-geography-16-5.s: Which of the following project – feature pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
o: Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi – Major Rayalaseema drought-mitigation project
Veligonda Project – Water supply to Chennai through Telugu Ganga
Galeru Nagari Sujala Sravanthi – Floodwater diversion to drought-prone areas
Kandaleru Project – Water supply to Chennai through Telugu Ganga
nap-geography-16-5.x: Veligonda has twin tunnels through the Srisailam–Nallamala region to Nallamala Sagar; Kandaleru is the Telugu Ganga link to Chennai.

nap-geography-12-7.s: Which of the following river – sea-mouth pairs is INCORRECTLY matched?
nap-geography-12-7.x: The Vamsadhara meets the sea at Kalingapatnam; Mopasu Bandar is the Nagavali's mouth.

nbf55fe0b4c2.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about projects on the Krishna river?
o: Srisailam is on the Nandyal side of the AP–Telangana region
Nagarjuna Sagar is situated near Nandikonda
Pulichintala is located in Palnadu district
Prakasam Barrage is located at Rajamahendravaram
nbf55fe0b4c2.x: Prakasam Barrage is at Vijayawada; the barrage at Rajamahendravaram is the Sir Arthur Cotton (Dowleswaram) Barrage on the Godavari.

n9141eab7561.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about the Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage?
o: It is located on the Vamsadhara River
It feeds the Eastern, Central and Western deltas
Its irrigation coverage is about 10.30 lakh acres
n9141eab7561.x: The Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage is on the Godavari, not the Vamsadhara.

n69f07beb7cb.s: Under the Bachawat Tribunal (KWDT-I), Andhra Pradesh's share of Krishna waters was:
n69f07beb7cb.x: AP's share was 811 TMC out of 2,060 TMC assessed at 75% dependability; the award came in 1976.

nap-geography-24-4.s: Which is the biggest tributary of the Tungabhadra?
nap-geography-24-4.x: The Hagari is the biggest tributary of the Tungabhadra.

nap-geography-16-19.s: The Sir Arthur Cotton Barrage at Rajamahendravaram is also called the:
nap-geography-16-19.x: The Cotton Barrage is also called the Dowleswaram Barrage; Prakasam Barrage is at Vijayawada.

nf8422dde044.s: While the Bahuda, Vamsadhara and Nagavali are covered by inter-state agreements, Godavari waters are governed through:
nf8422dde044.x: Godavari waters are governed through a tribunal award; Bahuda, Vamsadhara and Nagavali by inter-state agreements.

nbb86ef92746.s: Which of the following projects is objected to by Andhra Pradesh?
nbb86ef92746.x: AP objects to Kaleshwaram and Palamuru-Rangareddy; Telangana objects to Pattiseema, Polavaram and Banakacherla.

nb7d04c1fc9f.s: The Telugu Ganga Project, which takes Krishna water from Srisailam to Chennai, was conceived by:
nb7d04c1fc9f.x: Telugu Ganga was conceived by N. T. Rama Rao; it also irrigates 2.75 lakh acres in Kurnool and Kadapa.

n20d45924d49.s: When complete, the Veligonda (Nallamala Sagar) project is to irrigate about:
n20d45924d49.x: Veligonda is to irrigate about 4.47 lakh acres; its fluoride-free tap water is for western Prakasam.

n81997ebf583.s: About what share of Andhra Pradesh's area lies in the Godavari, Krishna and Pennar basins?
n81997ebf583.x: About 75% of AP lies in these three basins; AP has about 40 rivers, 15 of them inter-state.

nap-geography-3-17.s: The Somasila Dam on the Penna is located in which district?
nap-geography-3-17.x: Somasila is in Nellore; the Penna enters AP in Anantapur, cuts the Gandikota gorge in Kadapa and meets the sea at Utukuru.

nap-geography-22-7.s: The Kanithi Balancing Reservoir is located in:
nap-geography-22-7.x: Kanithi is in Visakhapatnam; Anantaraja Sagar is in Kadapa–Rajampeta, Cumbum Tank in Prakasam and Thimmaraju Cheruvu in Nandyal–Kurnool.

nfd95c9ca923.s: The Tungabhadra Dam, which feeds Andhra Pradesh's TBP-HLC, is located at:
nfd95c9ca923.x: The dam is at Hosapete in Karnataka on the Tungabhadra river, not the Penna.

nap-geography-8-4.s: The Machkund river originates in the:
nap-geography-8-4.x: The Madugula hills feed the Machkund; the Nandi hills the Papagni, the Jeypore hills the Vamsadhara and the Rayagada hills the Nagavali.

nap-geography-12-4.s: The Vasishta branch of the Godavari meets the sea at:
nap-geography-12-4.x: The Vasishta reaches the sea at Antarvedi; the Gautami at Yanam, the Krishna at Hamsaladeevi and the Champavathi at Konada.

n2c8f96f97f3.s: The Penna (Pennar) river rises in the:
n2c8f96f97f3.x: The Penna rises in the Nandidurga hills; 536 km of its 597 km lies in AP and it meets the sea at Utukuru.

n61dc6ae7003.s: Which scheme carries Godavari water to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage?
n61dc6ae7003.x: Pattiseema diverts Godavari water to the Krishna at Prakasam Barrage; Telugu Ganga serves Chennai, Rayalaseema and Nellore.

nea0bebef52e.s: In Dhurjati's works, the Swarnamukhi river is called:
nea0bebef52e.x: Dhurjati calls the Swarnamukhi 'Mogaleru'; Langulya is another name of the Nagavali.

na6b99733b38.s: The Kundu (Kunderu), a tributary of the Penna, is known as the 'Sorrow of':
na6b99733b38.x: The Kundu is the 'Sorrow of Nandyal'; it rises at Uppalapadu in Kurnool and its valley is called Renadu.

n6577e14dd72.s: The Sunkesula Barrage in Kurnool is on which river?
n6577e14dd72.x: Sunkesula Barrage is in Kurnool on the Tungabhadra; Somasila is the Nellore project.

nap-geography-12-8.s: The Gundlakamma river enters the sea at:
nap-geography-12-8.x: The Gundlakamma reaches the sea at Devarampadu; the Gosthani near Bheemunipatnam.

nap-geography-16-20.s: The Purushothapatnam Lift Irrigation Scheme transfers Godavari water to the:
nap-geography-16-20.x: It lifts Godavari water through the Polavaram Left Main Canal to the Yeleru, serving North Andhra and Visakhapatnam.

nap-geography-22-5.s: Thimmaraju Cheruvu was integrated with which modern reservoir system?
nap-geography-22-5.x: Thimmaraju Cheruvu joined the Owk Reservoir system; Anantaraja Sagar is a 14th-century Vijayanagara tank.

nap-geography-3-26.s: The 108 km long Arani river originates at:
nap-geography-3-26.x: The Arani rises at Sadasivakonda in Chittoor, flows south then east and joins the south-west tip of Pulicat Lake.

nap-geography-3-5.s: 'Langulya' is another name of which river?
nap-geography-3-5.x: Langulya is another name of the Nagavali.

nap-geography-11-5.s: The Veda and Avathi, rising in the Sahyadri, join to form the:
nap-geography-11-5.x: The Veda and Avathi rise in the eastern Sahyadri (Western Ghats) and join to form the Vedavathi.

nap-geography-16-14.s: The Right Main Canal of Nagarjuna Sagar, serving Guntur and Prakasam, is called the:
nap-geography-16-14.x: Nagarjuna Sagar's Right Main Canal is the Jawahar Canal, serving Guntur and Prakasam.

nap-geography-24-5.s: Which is the biggest and most important tributary of the Krishna?
nap-geography-24-5.x: The Tungabhadra is the Krishna's biggest tributary, and the Hagari is the Tungabhadra's biggest.

nap-geography-4-5.s: The Kundu joins the Penna at:
nap-geography-4-5.x: The Kundu joins the Penna at Adinimmayapalli; the Papagni joins near Kamalapuram and the Chitravathi at Gandikota.

nap-geography-3-21.s: The Nagavali river originates in the:
nap-geography-3-21.x: The Nagavali rises in Odisha's Rayagada hills and enters AP in Srikakulam district.

nap-geography-8-13.s: The Sabari river originates in the:
nap-geography-8-13.x: The Sabari rises in the Sinkaram hills of Odisha.

nap-geography-3-4.s: 'Pinakini' and 'Penneru' are other names of the:
nap-geography-3-4.x: The Penna is also called Pinakini and Penneru; it reaches the sea near Utukuru in Nellore.

n2c6a302e5e5.s: Which peninsular river has the largest basin?
n2c6a302e5e5.x: The Godavari has the largest peninsular basin, followed by the Krishna and the Mahanadi.

n83ab0fe278b.s: The Telugu Ganga route runs Srisailam – Somasila – Kandaleru and ends at which reservoir in Tamil Nadu?
n83ab0fe278b.x: The route runs from Srisailam through Somasila and Kandaleru to Poondi in Tamil Nadu.

nd60765f801c.s: The Polavaram Left Main Canal carries Godavari water towards:
nd60765f801c.x: The Polavaram Left Main Canal carries Godavari water to North Coastal Andhra and Visakhapatnam.

n55e4693b1b5.s: What is the design storage capacity of the Polavaram Project?
n55e4693b1b5.x: Polavaram's design: 194.6 TMC storage, 7.20 lakh acres irrigation, 960 MW and 80 TMC diversion to the Krishna.
